Rubber cultivation (Kerala specialty): Plant grafted stumps in June-July. Spacing 5x5m (400 trees/ha). Tapping starts 6-7 years. Yield 1500-2000 kg dry rubber/ha/year. Rainy climate essential!
Rubber varieties: RRII 105 (high yield, wind resistant), RRII 414, RRII 430, PB 260, GT 1. Choose based on wind exposure and soil type. RRII 105 most popular in Kerala!
Rubber tapping: Start when girth 50cm at 125cm height (6-7 years). Tap every alternate day (S/2 d2 system). Use proper knife angle (30°). Rainguard essential. Morning tapping best!
Rubber fertilizer (mature tree): 900g N, 400g P2O5, 900g K2O per tree per year in 2-3 splits (April-May, Sept-Oct). Apply in circular band 150cm from trunk!

Rubber diseases: Abnormal leaf fall (spray Bordeaux mixture before monsoon), Powdery mildew (Sulfur dust), Pink disease (scrape + Bordeaux paste), Root disease (remove infected). Preventive care crucial!
Kerala coconut varieties: West Coast Tall (WCT - most common), Chowghat Orange Dwarf (COD), Chowghat Green Dwarf (CGD), Lakshadweep Ordinary, Hybrid (DxT for higher yield)!
Coconut planting: Spacing 7.5-8m (175 palms/ha). Pit size 1x1x1m. Fill with topsoil + FYM + bone meal. Plant 10-12 month seedling. First yield 6-8 years (tall), 4-5 years (dwarf)!
Coconut fertilizer (adult palm): 500g N, 320g P2O5, 1200g K2O per palm per year in 2 splits (May-June, Sept-Oct). Apply in basin 1.8m from trunk. FYM 25kg/palm/year!
Coconut diseases Kerala: Root wilt (endemic, management only), Bud rot (Bordeaux spray + remove affected parts), Leaf rot (Carbendazim), Rhinoceros beetle (hook out + naphthalene balls)!
Improve coconut yield: Regular irrigation summer (40-50 nuts extra), Basin management, Integrated nutrient management, Intercropping (banana, pepper, cocoa), Mulching, Timely pest control!
Black pepper (King of Spices): Native to Kerala! Plant rooted cuttings in May-June. Support trees needed (Erythrina, Silver oak, Arecanut, Coconut). First yield 3-4 years!
Pepper varieties Kerala: Panniyur 1 (popular, high yield), Karimunda (traditional, quality), IISR Shakti, IISR Thevam, Sreekara. Panniyur 1 most widely planted!
Pepper planting: 2-3 rooted cuttings per standard. Spacing based on support - Arecanut 2.7m, Erythrina 3m. Tie vines initially. Snake coil pruning improves yield!
Pepper diseases: Quick wilt (Phytophthora - most serious, Metalaxyl drench + drainage), Slow wilt (nematodes - Carbofuran), Pollu disease (Bordeaux spray), Anthracnose!
Pepper fertilizer per vine: 50g N, 50g P2O5, 150g K2O (adult vine) in 2-3 splits. Apply May-June and Sept-Oct. Organic matter (FYM/compost) essential. Mulching helps!
Cardamom (Queen of Spices): Shade-loving crop. Grown in Western Ghats (Idukki, Wayanad). Spacing 2x2m. First yield 3rd year. Peak 7-15 years. High value Rs.1000-2000/kg!
Cardamom varieties: Malabar (traditional, green capsules), Mysore (vigorous, high yield), Vazhukka (hybrid character). PV1, PV2, ICRI varieties disease resistant!
Cardamom planting: Plant seedlings/suckers June-July. Partial shade essential (40-60%). Raised beds in waterlogged areas. Rich humus soil required. High rainfall areas ideal!
Cardamom diseases: Katte/Mosaic virus (remove infected plants, control aphids), Capsule rot/Azhukal (Bordeaux spray), Rhizome rot (improve drainage, Trichoderma), Thrips (Spinosad)!
Cardamom care: Maintain shade trees, Mulching with leaves, Trashing (remove old shoots), Irrigate in dry months, Harvest when capsules green and firm. Dry to 10% moisture!
Arecanut cultivation: Plant seedlings June-July. Spacing 2.7x2.7m (1360 palms/ha). First yield 6-7 years. Long productive life (50+ years). Shade loving initially!
Arecanut varieties: Mangala (high yield), Sumangala, Shreemangala, South Kanara, Mohitnagar. Choose disease-tolerant varieties for Kerala conditions!
Arecanut fertilizer: Adult palm - 100g N, 40g P2O5, 140g K2O per palm per year in 2 splits. FYM 12kg/palm. Apply in basin. Organic matter very important!
Arecanut diseases: Koleroga/Mahali (fruit rot - Bordeaux mixture before monsoon), Yellow leaf disease (management only - improve nutrition, drainage), Inflorescence dieback!
Arecanut processing: Harvest when ripe (green to yellow). Boil + dry (Chali), or peel + dry (white supari). Different grades for different markets. Processing adds value!
Cashew cultivation: Plant grafted plants June-July. Spacing 8x8m (156 trees/ha). First yield 3rd year (grafted). Tolerates poor/laterite soil. Low maintenance!
Cashew varieties: BPP-8 (high yield), Vengurla-4, Priyanka, Dhana, Ullal-1. Choose based on kernel quality and yield. BPP-8 popular in Kerala!
Cashew fertilizer: Adult tree - 500g N, 125g P2O5, 125g K2O per tree per year. Apply before monsoon (May-June). Organic matter improves soil in laterite areas!
Cashew pests: Tea mosquito bug (major - spray Carbaryl at flowering), Stem borer (clean hole, inject petrol + plug), Flower thrips (Spinosad spray). Monitor during flowering!
Cashew apple: Fleshy fruit attached to nut. Makes juice, feni, jam. Often wasted! Value addition opportunity. Raw nut yields 25-30% kernel after processing!
Nutmeg cultivation: Tropical spice, Kerala specialty! Plant seedlings/grafts June-July. Spacing 8x8m. Dioecious (male + female trees). First yield 6-8 years. Shade tolerant!
Nutmeg propagation: Seed (uncertain sex, late bearing), Epicotyl grafting (early bearing, known sex). Plant 1 male per 10 females for pollination. Grafted plants preferred!
Nutmeg yield: Mature tree gives 1000-2000 fruits/year. Two products - Nutmeg (seed) and Mace (aril covering). Both high value. Peak bearing 20-30 years!
Nutmeg processing: Harvest when fruit splits. Remove fleshy pericarp (can make pickle). Separate mace from seed. Dry separately. Mace turns reddish-orange when dry!
Nutmeg care: Partial shade beneficial, Regular irrigation, Mulching important, Fruit rot (remove affected fruits), Thread blight (Bordeaux spray). Low maintenance once established!
Clove cultivation: Tropical evergreen, suited for Kerala highlands. Plant seedlings June-July. Spacing 6-7m. First flowering 7-8 years. Long-lived (100+ years)!
Clove planting: Partial shade needed initially. Well-drained soil essential. Pit size 75x75x75cm. Needs high rainfall + humidity. Idukki, Kottayam, Trivandrum districts!
Clove harvest: Harvest unopened flower buds (before pink stage). Hand-picking. 4-5 harvests/year during season (Sept-Feb). Yield 2-5 kg dry cloves/tree!
Clove processing: Dry harvested buds in sun 4-5 days to 10% moisture. Color changes from reddish to dark brown. Store in airtight containers. High value spice!
Clove problems: Seedling blight (Carbendazim), Leaf spot, Stem borer. Generally hardy once established. Frost sensitive - not for very high altitudes!
Vanilla cultivation: High-value orchid crop! Plant cuttings June-July on support trees (Gliricidia, Erythrina). Spacing 2.5x2.5m. First flowering 3rd year. Needs shade!
Vanilla pollination: Critical! Hand-pollinate each flower (morning 6-11 AM). Flowers open only one day. Skill required. Without pollination, no beans! Labor intensive!
Vanilla curing: Beans harvested 9 months after pollination. Complex curing process (killing, sweating, drying, conditioning) takes 6 months. Determines quality!
Vanilla problems: Root rot (drainage + Trichoderma), Stem rot, Viral diseases (remove infected). High management, high risk, high reward crop!
Vanilla economics: Very high value (Rs.25,000-40,000/kg cured beans). But labor-intensive pollination, skill-intensive curing. Not for beginners. Start small, learn, then scale!
Cocoa cultivation: Excellent intercrop in coconut/arecanut! Shade-loving crop. Plant seedlings June-July. Spacing 2.7x2.7m as intercrop. First pod 3rd year!
Cocoa varieties: Forastero (common, hardy), Criollo (fine flavor, delicate), Trinitario (hybrid). CCRP varieties from CPCRI recommended for Kerala!
Cocoa as intercrop: Perfect under coconut (75-100 plants/ha), arecanut, rubber. Additional income Rs.15,000-25,000/ha from existing plantation. Win-win!
Cocoa harvest: Pods ripen 5-6 months after pollination. Harvest when color changes (green to yellow/red). 2-3 harvests/year. Extract beans, ferment, dry!
Cocoa processing: Break pod → Extract beans → Ferment 5-7 days (flavor development) → Dry to 7% moisture → Sell to buyers. Fermentation critical for quality!
Coffee cultivation Kerala: Wayanad main district. Robusta (lowlands, 90%) and Arabica (highlands, 10%). Shade-grown under native trees. Planted June-July!
Coffee varieties: Robusta - CxR, S-274 (high yield). Arabica - S-795, Chandragiri, Selection-9 (disease resistant). Choose based on altitude!
Coffee planting: Spacing 3x3m Robusta, 2x2m Arabica. Shade trees essential (Silver oak, Dadap). Pit size 45x45x45cm. Rain-fed in Kerala (2000-3000mm)!
Coffee diseases: Coffee leaf rust (Bordeaux spray), Black rot (shade management), White stem borer (remove affected, lime paste on stems), Berry borer (timely harvest)!
Coffee processing: Cherry picking (ripe red berries) → Pulping → Fermentation → Washing → Drying (parchment) → Hulling → Grading. Quality depends on processing!
Tea cultivation Kerala: High ranges of Idukki (Munnar), Wayanad. Altitude 1000-2000m. Cool climate essential. Acid soil (pH 4.5-5.5). High rainfall areas!
Tea planting: Vegetatively propagated (cuttings). Spacing 1.2x0.6m (13,500 plants/ha). Contour planting on slopes. Shade trees (Silver oak, Grevillea) at intervals!
Tea plucking: Pluck 2 leaves + bud every 7-10 days during season. Fine plucking for quality, coarse plucking for quantity. Manual plucking in Kerala (quality tea)!
Tea pruning: Medium prune (5-year cycle) rejuvenates bush. Skiffing (light) annual. Centering for young plants. Proper pruning maintains productivity!
Tea processing: Withering → Rolling → Oxidation (fermentation) → Drying → Sorting → Grading. Orthodox method in Kerala hills. CTC in some areas. Processing determines tea type!
Kuttanad - Unique farming: World's only region farming below sea level (-2.2m)! In Alappuzha, Kerala. UNESCO designated 'Globally Important Agricultural Heritage System'!
Kuttanad system: Bunds (dykes) protect fields from backwaters. Pump out water. Single rice crop (Puncha - Aug-March). Summer - fish/prawn in same fields!
Kuttanad rice varieties: Jyothi (HYV, common), Uma, Vyttila, Traditional varieties (Chovvarian, Thavalakannan). Flood-tolerant varieties important!
Kuttanad challenges: Salinity intrusion, Waterlogging, Acidity, High input cost (pumping, bunding). Labor intensive. But traditional knowledge sustains it!
Pokkali cultivation: Another unique Kerala system. Salt-tolerant rice in coastal areas (Ernakulam). Rice-prawn rotation. Traditional organic system. GI registered!
Kerala homestead (Parambu): Traditional multi-tier farming around homes. Coconut (top tier), Arecanut/Jackfruit (middle), Pepper/Banana/Cocoa (lower), Vegetables (ground). Maximum use of space!
Multi-tier system: Coconut (8m) → Arecanut (6m) → Clove/Nutmeg (4m) → Pepper (climber) → Banana/Cocoa (2-3m) → Pineapple/Tapioca → Vegetables/Turmeric. 5-7 crops on same land!
Homestead advantages: Diverse income, Food security, Year-round harvest, Risk distribution, Ecological benefits, Low external inputs. Traditional Kerala wisdom!
Homestead vegetables: Grow on available space. Amaranthus, Snake gourd, Bitter gourd, Chili, Brinjal, Drumstick, Curry leaf, Coriander. Fresh, pesticide-free!
Livestock integration: Cow/goats + poultry part of homestead. Manure for plants, milk/eggs for family, crop residue for feed. Closed-loop system!
Kerala banana varieties: Nendran (plantain, chips, most commercial), Poovan (Mysore, eating), Palayankodan (dwarf Cavendish), Robusta, Red banana, Njalipoovan. Nendran most valuable!
Nendran cultivation: Plant suckers/TC plants. Spacing 2x2m. Duration 11-14 months. Single bunch per plant. Famous for chips. Kerala's signature banana!
Banana fertilizer Kerala: Per plant - 100g N + 30g P2O5 + 250g K2O in 6-8 monthly splits. FYM 10kg at planting. Potassium very important for Nendran!
Banana diseases Kerala: Bunchy top virus (roguing + aphid control), Panama wilt (resistant varieties), Sigatoka (dithane spray), Rhizome rot (avoid waterlogging)!
Banana intercropping: Excellent under coconut/arecanut. Also grows well with ginger, turmeric, vegetables in initial months. Additional income from existing plantation!
Pineapple Kerala: Major producer! Vazhakulam (Ernakulam) famous. GI tagged 'Vazhakulam Pineapple'. Grown as intercrop or monocrop. Duration 18-24 months for first harvest!
Pineapple varieties: Kew (common, processing), Mauritius (fresh eating, less fiber), MD2 (export quality, sweet, new introduction), Giant Kew. Kew dominates Kerala!
Pineapple planting: Plant suckers/slips. Spacing 25x60x90cm (double row). Plant June-July or Sept-Oct. 44,000-50,000 plants/ha. Partial shade beneficial!
Pineapple fertilizer: 12g N + 4g P2O5 + 12g K2O per plant per year in 6 splits. Apply as soil drenching. Potassium improves fruit quality!
Pineapple forcing: Induce flowering with Ethrel (25ppm spray) or Calcium carbide (in leaf whorl). Synchronizes harvest for market. Apply at 12-14 months!
Tapioca (Cassava): Kerala staple! Easy crop, tolerates poor soil, drought. Plant setts (stem cuttings) April-May or Sept-Oct. Duration 10-12 months!
Tapioca varieties: H-165, H-226, Sree Visakham, Sree Sahya, Sree Prakash. H-165, H-226 popular for eating. Sree varieties for starch. Choose based on use!
Tapioca planting: 20cm sett with 4-5 buds. Spacing 90x90cm. Plant horizontally or slanted (not vertical). Ridges help in waterlogged areas!
Tapioca fertilizer: 100kg N, 50kg P2O5, 100kg K2O per hectare in 2 splits (45 and 90 days). FYM 12.5 tons/ha. Potassium important for tuber quality!
Tapioca diseases: Mosaic virus (resistant varieties), Tuber rot (drainage, crop rotation), Mites (Dicofol spray). Generally hardy crop. Good for marginal lands!
Ginger (Inji) Kerala: Shade-tolerant, excellent intercrop. Wayanad, Idukki main areas. Plant April-May. Duration 8-9 months. Mulching essential!
Ginger varieties Kerala: Maran, Rio-de-Janeiro, Nadia, Kuruppampady, IISR Varada, IISR Mahima. Maran and Kuruppampady traditional, high oleoresin!
Turmeric (Manjal) Kerala: Similar to ginger. Plant April-May. Duration 7-9 months. Varieties - Alleppey, Ernakulam, Wayanad local, IISR Prabha, IISR Pratibha!
Disease management: Soft rot (Rhizome rot) - most serious! Seed treatment with Trichoderma, good drainage, crop rotation. Avoid infected rhizomes!
Intercropping system: Ginger/Turmeric under coconut, arecanut, banana. Uses partial shade, additional income. Apply fertilizer separately for each crop!
Kerala vegetables: Amaranthus (Cheera), Snake gourd, Bitter gourd, Ash gourd, Cucumber, Cowpea, Drumstick, Brinjal, Okra, Ivy gourd. Suited to humid climate!
Monsoon vegetables: Amaranthus (easy, quick), Cowpea, Cucumber, Ash gourd thrive in rainy season. Use raised beds for drainage. Avoid waterlogging!
Snake gourd: Sow April-May or Sept-Oct. Pandal/trellis system. Duration 60-70 days to first harvest. Train on bower. Pick young for tenderness!
Bitter gourd: Sow Feb-March or June-July. Trellis essential. Pick green, before yellowing. High demand, good price. Preethi, Priyanka varieties!
Vegetable challenges Kerala: High humidity (disease pressure), Pest problems (fruit fly, borers), Competition from other states. Focus on quality, local markets!
Rice-fish/prawn system: Traditional in Kuttanad, Pokkali areas. Rice during monsoon, fish/prawn during summer in same fields. Integrated, sustainable, profitable!
Pokkali system: Unique rice-prawn rotation in Ernakulam, Thrissur coast. Organic rice (no chemicals), followed by prawn/fish. GI registered. High value!
Prawn farming: Penaeus monodon (Tiger prawn), P. indicus (Indian white). Extensive/traditional or semi-intensive. Good returns but needs management!
Karimeen (Pearl spot): Kerala's state fish! Farmed in backwaters, ponds. Excellent price (Rs.400-600/kg). Grows well in brackish water!
Integration: Fish in farm ponds (irrigation + fish income), Rice-fish (pest control + protein), Coconut garden ponds (nutrient recycling). Multiple benefits!
Organic farming Kerala: Government promotes through various schemes. PGS-India (Participatory Guarantee System) for domestic market certification. Group-based, affordable!
Kerala organic crops: Spices (cardamom, pepper, ginger, turmeric), Coffee (Wayanad), Vegetables, Coconut. Premium markets in metros, exports!
Certification: NPOP for export (costly), PGS-India for domestic (affordable, group-based). Register at pgsindia.org. Training through KVK, agriculture dept!
Organic inputs: Jeevamrut, Panchagavya, Vermicompost, Neem products, Trichoderma, Pseudomonas. Kerala Agriculture University recommendations available!
Marketing: Organic stores (many in cities), Weekly organic markets (Thiruvananthapuram, Kochi, Kozhikode), Online platforms, FPO collective marketing!
Kerala has 2 monsoons: Southwest (June-Sept, heavy) and Northeast (Oct-Nov, lighter). Cropping planned around this. Very different from North India!
Rice seasons Kerala: Virippu (April-Sept, monsoon crop), Mundakan (Sept-Dec/Jan, second crop), Puncha (Dec-March, summer, Kuttanad). 3 crops where water available!
Monsoon planting: Banana, Ginger, Turmeric, Pepper, all spices planted with monsoon onset (May-June). Uses natural irrigation. Critical timing!
Monsoon challenges: Waterlogging (drainage!), Disease pressure (fungal diseases rampant), Pest buildup, Difficult spraying. Preventive measures important!
Monsoon opportunities: Natural irrigation (no cost), Best planting time for most crops, Green manuring, Soil building. Plan and prepare before monsoon!
Labor shortage: Major issue! High wages (Rs.800-1000/day), labor migration to Gulf. Mechanization difficult in small, sloped, mixed farms. Need labor-saving technologies!
High cost: Input costs high, labor expensive, small holdings (avg. 0.2 ha), fragmented land. Returns often don't match investment. Diversification needed!
Competition: Vegetables, fruits from Tamil Nadu, Karnataka cheaper. Local production costly. Focus on quality, local/organic markets, value addition!
Wildlife damage: Elephants, wild boar increasing problem near forests. Compensation inadequate. Fencing expensive. Farmer-wildlife conflict growing!
Solutions: Mechanization, Group farming (FPOs), Value addition, Organic premium markets, Agri-tourism, Niche crops (spices, medicinal plants). Adapt and diversify!
Subhiksha Keralam: State scheme for vegetable self-sufficiency. Subsidies for seeds, inputs, infrastructure. Promotes homestead vegetable cultivation!
Coconut Development Board: Replanting subsidy, Coconut palm insurance, Neera/Coconut sugar promotion, Technology mission. Check cdb.nic.in!
Spices Board: Subsidies for spice cultivation (cardamom, pepper, ginger), Organic certification support, Quality improvement, Export promotion. spices.board.in!

Photosynthesis: Plants convert CO2 + H2O → Glucose + O2 using sunlight. C3 plants (rice, wheat): Calvin cycle directly. C4 plants (maize, sugarcane): additional step, more efficient in heat!
Nitrogen fixation: Conversion of atmospheric N2 to plant-usable forms. Biological (Rhizobium in legume root nodules), or industrial (fertilizers). Legumes fix 50-200 kg N/ha!
Plant hormones: Auxins (growth, rooting), Gibberellins (elongation, flowering), Cytokinins (cell division), Ethylene (ripening), ABA (stress response). Applied in agriculture for various purposes!
Photoperiodism: Plant response to day length. Short-day plants (rice) flower when days shorten. Long-day plants (wheat) need long days. Day-neutral (tomato) flower regardless!
Vernalization: Cold requirement for flowering. Some crops (wheat, onion for seed) need cold period to flower. Important for variety selection based on climate!
Fertilizer calculation: If 120kg N/ha recommended and Urea is 46% N, then Urea needed = 120/0.46 = 261 kg/ha. For acre: 261/2.47 = 106 kg/acre. Always calculate based on nutrient content!
Plant population: Plants/ha = 10000 ÷ (row spacing m × plant spacing m). Example: 60×45cm = 10000 ÷ (0.6×0.45) = 37,037 plants/ha. Per acre: divide by 2.47!
Spray solution: If 2ml pesticide per liter recommended, and sprayer tank is 16L, then add 2×16 = 32ml pesticide per tank. Always follow label instructions!
Water requirement: ET0 × Kc × Area = Water need. Drip efficiency 90% vs flood 50%. So drip needs less water for same crop water need. Measure with pan evaporation locally!
Cost-benefit ratio: Total returns ÷ Total costs. If expenditure Rs.50,000 and income Rs.80,000, CBR = 80000/50000 = 1.6. Higher than 1 is profitable!

Kerala water paradox: High rainfall (3000mm) but summer water scarcity! Water runs off quickly in laterite terrain. Rainwater harvesting, farm ponds essential!
Farm ponds Kerala: Lined ponds (silpaulin/HDPE) for laterite areas. Government subsidy under MGNREGA, Jalanidhi. Store monsoon water for summer irrigation!
Groundwater recharging: Open wells, percolation pits, contour bunds on slopes. Kerala terrain allows good recharge if structures in place. Plan before monsoon!
Summer irrigation: Critical for coconut, arecanut, banana, vegetables (March-May). Drip irrigation saves water 60-70%. Basin irrigation for coconut!
Water budgeting: Measure monsoon rainfall, calculate runoff, plan storage. Even small pond (10x10x3m = 300 cubic meters) can irrigate 0.5 acre vegetables in summer!
Kerala soil types: Laterite (65%, hilly/midlands), Alluvial (coastal, river valleys), Forest soil (Western Ghats), Coastal sandy, Kuttanad peaty clay!
Laterite soil: Red, acidic (pH 5-6), low fertility, good drainage. Dominant in Kerala. Needs lime, organic matter. Suits rubber, coconut, cashew, tapioca!
Improving laterite: Add lime (correct acidity), FYM/compost (improve fertility + structure), green manuring, mulching. Regular organic matter addition essential!
Coastal sandy soil: Low water/nutrient retention. Add organic matter, clay if available. Coconut, cashew, casuarina suited. Salinity issue near sea!
Kuttanad soil: Peaty, acidic, waterlogged. Unique management - bunding, pumping, acid-tolerant varieties. Challenging but productive when managed well!
Major pests Kerala: Rhinoceros beetle & Red palm weevil (coconut, arecanut), Fruit fly (vegetables, fruits), Coffee berry borer, Tea mosquito bug (cashew)!
Coconut pests: Rhinoceros beetle (hook out + naphthalene), Red palm weevil (pheromone trap + injection), Eriophyid mite (spray wettable sulfur). Regular monitoring!
Quick wilt pepper: Phytophthora infection. Symptoms: sudden wilting, black roots. Control: Drainage, Metalaxyl drench, Trichoderma, avoid waterlogging. Remove infected vines!
Root wilt coconut: Endemic disease, no cure. Management: Improve nutrition, drainage, apply recommended fertilizers. Tolerant varieties: Chowghat Green Dwarf!
Fruit fly: Major pest of vegetables, mango, guava. Control: Methyl eugenol traps, bait spray, fruit bagging, field sanitation. IPM approach essential!
Kerala mechanization challenges: Small holdings, sloped terrain, mixed cropping. Full mechanization difficult. Need adapted small machines!
Suitable machines: Power tiller (versatile, small farms), Mini tractor (4WD for slopes), Brush cutter, Power sprayer, Coconut climber, Chaff cutter!
Coconut climber: Solves labor problem! Various models available (Rs.3000-15000). Training needed. Government subsidy available. Useful innovation!
Custom hiring: Don't buy expensive machines - rent from CHC (Custom Hiring Center). Combine harvester, transplanter available at block level!

Rice cultivation: Kharif crop (June-Nov). Prepare nursery in May-June, transplant after 25-30 days. Main varieties: Basmati (120-140 days), IR64 (115 days), Swarna (140-145 days). Needs: flooded fields, 20-25°C temperature!

Dhan ki kheti: 1) Nursery preparation (May-June), 2) Puddling (wet tillage), 3) Transplanting (2-3 seedlings/hill, 20x15cm spacing), 4) Water management (keep flooded), 5) Fertilizer: 120kg N, 60kg P2O5, 40kg K2O per hectare!

Rice varieties for South Asia: Basmati 370 (premium, aromatic), IRRI-6 (high yield), Super Basmati (export quality), Kainaat (disease resistant), Shandar (short duration). Choose based on soil type and market!
Rice water management: Keep 5-7cm standing water during vegetative stage, 2-3cm during flowering, drain 10 days before harvest. Total water need: 1200-1500mm!
Direct seeded rice (DSR): Sow dry/pre-germinated seeds directly in field. Advantages: saves water (25-30%), no transplanting labor, early maturity (7-10 days). Use weed management carefully!

Wheat cultivation (Rabi crop): Sowing October-November, harvest March-April. Seed rate: 100kg/hectare for timely sowing, 125kg for late. Spacing: 20-22cm row spacing. Needs 4-6 irrigations throughout growing period!

Gehun ki kheti: Popular varieties - HD2967, PBW343, DBW17, WH1105. Fertilizer: 120kg N (half at sowing, half at first irrigation), 60kg P2O5, 40kg K2O per hectare. First irrigation at CRI stage (20-25 days)!

Wheat irrigation schedule: 1st - Crown Root Initiation (20-25 days), 2nd - Tillering (40-45 days), 3rd - Jointing (60-65 days), 4th - Flowering (80-85 days), 5th - Milk stage (100-105 days), 6th - Dough stage (115-120 days)!
Best wheat varieties: HD3086 (heat tolerant), PBW725 (rust resistant), DBW222 (high yield), WH1124 (chapati quality), Lok-1 (rainfed areas). Choose based on your region's climate!
Wheat diseases & control: Rust (fungicide spray - Propiconazole), Karnal bunt (seed treatment - Tebuconazole), Loose smut (hot water seed treatment 4hrs at 45°C). Use resistant varieties!

Basmati rice: Premium aromatic variety, 130-145 day duration. Transplanting in June-July, harvest October-November. Spacing: 20x15cm. Varieties: Pusa Basmati 1121 (longest grain), 1509 (early), Traditional 370 (authentic aroma)!

Basmati cultivation tips: Use aged seeds (1 year old) for better aroma and cooking quality. Apply less nitrogen (80-100kg/ha) to maintain grain quality. Drain field 2 weeks before harvest for better milling!
Basmati varieties: Pusa 1121 (125-130 days, 8.3mm cooked length), Pusa 1509 (120 days, early), CSR-30 (saline tolerant), Pusa Basmati 6 (bacterial blight resistant). Choose certified seeds only!

Basmati fertilizer: 100kg N, 50kg P2O5, 50kg K2O per hectare. Apply nitrogen in splits: 50% at transplanting, 25% at tillering, 25% at panicle initiation. Use FYM 10 tons/hectare before transplanting!
Basmati export quality tips: Proper drying (12-13% moisture), aging minimum 1 year, avoid mixing varieties, control weeds (affects purity), harvest at right maturity (80% grain golden yellow)!

Mango cultivation: Plant grafted saplings in July-August (monsoon). Spacing: 10x10m for high-density, 5x5m for ultra-high density. Varieties: Alphonso (Konkan), Dasheri (UP), Langra (Bihar), Kesar (Gujarat), Chaunsa (Punjab)!
Aam ki kheti: Fertilizer per tree - Year 1: 10kg FYM + 100g N, P, K each. Increase annually. Mature tree (10+ years): 50kg FYM + 1.5kg N, 0.75kg P2O5, 1.5kg K2O. Apply in two splits (June & October)!

Mango varieties: Alphonso (export quality, sweet), Dasheri (North India favorite), Kesar (saffron aroma), Totapuri (pickle variety), Banganpalli (South India), Langra (fiber-less), Amrapali (dwarf, high density)!
Mango diseases: Powdery mildew (spray Sulfex 0.2%), Anthracnose (Copper oxychloride 0.3%), Mango hopper (Imidacloprid spray at flowering). Spray before monsoon and after fruit set!
Mango flowering: Flowering November-February. Apply Paclobutrazol (soil drenching) in September-October to promote uniform flowering. Spray NAA 20ppm during peak flowering to reduce fruit drop!

Banana cultivation: Plant tissue culture plants in Feb-March or June-July. Spacing: 1.8x1.8m (3086 plants/hectare). Varieties: Grand Naine (export), Robusta (common), Nendran (Kerala), Red banana, Poovan!
Kela ki kheti: Fertilizer per plant - 200g N, 60g P2O5, 300g K2O in 8-10 splits. Apply every month. Needs regular irrigation (4-5 days interval). Bunchy top virus: remove infected plants immediately!
Banana varieties: Grand Naine (Cavendish, export quality, 12-13 months), Robusta (common, hardy, 12-15 months), Poovan (Mysore, small sweet), Nendran (cooking, Kerala), Red banana (premium)!
Tissue culture banana benefits: Disease-free, uniform growth, higher yield (40-50 kg/plant vs 25-30 kg conventional), early bearing (11-12 months). Initial cost higher but better returns!
Banana diseases: Panama wilt (use resistant variety), Sigatoka (spray Carbendazim), Bunchy top virus (remove infected plants + control aphids), Pseudostem weevil (apply Carbofuran in soil)!

Tomato cultivation: Kharif (June-July), Rabi (October-November), Summer (January-February). Hybrid varieties: Arka Rakshak, Arka Samrat, US 618, Namdhari 777. Spacing: 60x45cm. Transplant 25-30 day seedlings!

Tamatar ki kheti: Fertilizer - 150kg N, 75kg P2O5, 75kg K2O per hectare. Apply FYM 25 tons at field preparation. Nitrogen in splits: 50% basal, 25% at 30 days, 25% at flowering. Need staking for hybrid varieties!
Tomato diseases: Early blight (Mancozeb 0.25%), Late blight (Cymoxanil+Mancozeb), Leaf curl virus (control whitefly with Imidacloprid), Bacterial wilt (use resistant variety + soil solarization)!

Hybrid tomato varieties: Arka Rakshak F1 (bacterial wilt resistant, 70-75 tons/ha), Arka Samrat (nematode resistant), Pusa Hybrid 4 (heat tolerant), Naveen 2000 (long shelf life), Abhilash (determinate)!

Tomato care: Mulching with paddy straw, drip irrigation (reduce water 30%), remove suckers (for indeterminate types), stake plants, spray calcium for preventing blossom end rot. Pick fruits at breaker stage for market!

Potato cultivation: Rabi crop, October-November planting. Use certified seed potatoes (2-2.5 tons/hectare). Spacing: 60x20cm. Earthing up 30 days after planting. Varieties: Kufri Jyoti (90-100 days), Kufri Pukhraj (90 days), Kufri Bahar (110 days)!
Aloo ki kheti: Fertilizer - 180kg N, 80kg P2O5, 100kg K2O per hectare. Apply full P&K + 1/3 N at planting, remaining N in 2 splits (30 & 45 days). Need 5-6 irrigations during growing period!
Potato varieties: Kufri Jyoti (early, table purpose, 250-300 q/ha), Kufri Pukhraj (chips making), Kufri Chandramukhi (processing), Kufri Badshah (late blight resistant), Kufri Ashoka (heat tolerant)!

Potato late blight control: Most serious disease! Spray Mancozeb (0.25%) or Metalaxyl+Mancozeb at 10-day intervals during cool humid weather. Use resistant varieties like Kufri Giriraj. Remove infected plants!

Seed potato treatment: Treat with Mancozeb (2.5g/liter) before planting. Use small tubers (30-40g) or cut large ones with 2-3 eyes. Dry cut pieces 2-3 days before planting. Chitting (sprouting) improves emergence!

Onion cultivation: Kharif (June-July), Rabi (Nov-Dec), Late Kharif (Sept-Oct). Transplant 40-45 day seedlings. Spacing: 15x10cm. Varieties: Pusa Red (Kharif), N-53 (Rabi), Bhima Shakti (export). Duration: 120-150 days!
Pyaz ki kheti: Fertilizer - 100kg N, 50kg P2O5, 50kg K2O per hectare. Apply full P&K + 1/2 N at transplanting, remaining N in 2 splits (30 & 45 days). Needs light frequent irrigation (7-10 days)!

Onion varieties: Pusa Red (dark red, kharif), N-53 (yellow, rabi, good storage), Bhima Super (white, export), Agrifound Dark Red (rabi), Bhima Shakti (late kharif, purple), Bhima Kiran (white multiplier)!

Onion diseases: Purple blotch (Mancozeb spray), Stemphylium blight (Azoxystrobin), Thrips (Fipronil spray), Basal rot (use healthy sets, avoid water logging). Stop irrigation 15 days before harvest for better storage!
Onion storage: Cure bulbs in shade 10-15 days, store in ventilated room, maintain 25-30°C & 60-70% humidity. Properly cured onions last 3-4 months. N-53 and Agrifound varieties store best!

Chili cultivation: Kharif (June-July) for dry chili, All year for green. Transplant 30-35 day seedlings. Spacing: 60x45cm. Varieties: Byadgi (Karnataka), Guntur Sannam (AP), Pusa Jwala (green), Wonder Hot (hybrid)!

Mirch ki kheti: Fertilizer - 150kg N, 75kg P2O5, 75kg K2O per hectare. Apply FYM 20-25 tons. Nitrogen in 4-5 splits. Needs regular irrigation but avoid water logging. Harvest green at 45 days, red at 80-90 days!

Chili varieties: Byadgi (paprika, deep red color), Guntur Sannam (high pungency, export), Teja (super hot, high yield), Pusa Jwala (green chili), Wonder Hot (hybrid, virus resistant), Kashmiri (mild, color)!
Chili diseases: Leaf curl virus (control whitefly + roguing), Anthracnose (fruit rot - Copper oxychloride), Powdery mildew (Sulfur spray), Die back (Bordeaux mixture). Use virus-resistant hybrids!

Chili drying: Dry red chilies in sun 7-10 days to 10% moisture. Proper drying prevents aflatoxin. Store in gunny bags in dry place. Dry chili yield: 15-20 quintals/hectare, Green: 100-150 quintals/hectare!

Cotton cultivation: Kharif crop (May-June). Varieties: BT cotton hybrids (Bollgard II), Desi cotton varieties. Spacing: 90x60cm for hybrids, 45x30cm for desi. Needs 5-6 irrigations. Duration: 150-180 days!

Kapas ki kheti: Fertilizer - 120kg N, 60kg P2O5, 60kg K2O per hectare for hybrids. Apply nitrogen in 3 splits (basal, squaring, flowering). Use FYM 10 tons. Critical irrigation at flowering and boll development!

BT cotton: Genetically modified for bollworm resistance (Bollgard II - dual gene). Varieties: RCH-2, Ankur-651, MRC-7361. Higher yield (25-30 quintals/ha vs 15-20 desi). Still need IPM for sucking pests!
Cotton pests: Pink bollworm (pheromone traps + Bt spray), Whitefly (Thiamethoxam), Jassids (Imidacloprid), American bollworm (NPV + Bt on non-BT). Follow refuge strategy for BT cotton (20% non-BT)!
Cotton harvesting: Pick when 50-60% bolls open. Multiple pickings (3-4 times) for better quality. Kapas (seed cotton) yield: 20-25 quintals/hectare (hybrids), 35% ginning outturn. Store in dry place!

Sugarcane cultivation: Plant Feb-March (spring) or Sept-Oct (autumn). Use 3-bud setts (2-3 tons/hectare). Spacing: 90cm rows. Varieties: Co 0238 (early), CoJ 64 (mid), Co 118 (late). Duration: 10-12 months (plant), 12 months (ratoon)!

Ganna ki kheti: Fertilizer - Plant crop: 150kg N, 60kg P2O5, 60kg K2O per hectare. Ratoon: 180kg N. Apply nitrogen in 3 splits (planting, 60 days, 120 days). Need 10-12 irrigations. Earthing up at 90-120 days!

Sugarcane varieties: CoJ 64 (mid-late, high sugar), Co 0238 (early, 10 months), Co 118 (waterlogging tolerant), CoLk 94184 (salt tolerant), Co 86032 (disease resistant). Choose based on harvest time and soil!

Sugarcane diseases: Red rot (most serious - use resistant variety + Carbendazim), Smut (remove whips + spray Propiconazole), Wilt (soil treatment), Grassy shoot (control leafhopper). Use disease-free seed setts!

Ratoon management: After harvest, gap filling within 15 days. Apply fertilizer (higher nitrogen). Light irrigation immediately. Trash mulching beneficial. First ratoon gives 80-90% plant crop yield. Take 3-4 ratoons!

Mustard cultivation: Rabi crop (Oct-Nov sowing). Varieties: Pusa Bold (95-100 days), Varuna (125-130 days), RH 30 (brown, 130 days). Seed rate: 4-5 kg/hectare. Spacing: 30-45cm rows. Harvest when pods turn yellowish-brown!

Sarson ki kheti: Fertilizer - 100-120kg N, 40kg P2O5, 20kg K2O per hectare. Apply half nitrogen at sowing, half at 30-35 days. Needs 2-3 irrigations (pre-flowering & pod filling). Thinning at 20-25 days!

Mustard varieties: Pusa Bold (yellow, early, 18-20q/ha), Varuna (brown, late, high oil), Pusa Mustard 25 (aphid tolerant), RH 30 (brown sarson), Kranti (white rust resistant), Pusa Agrani (early 90 days)!
Mustard diseases: White rust (spray Metalaxyl), Alternaria blight (Mancozeb), Powdery mildew (Sulfur). Aphids major pest - spray Dimethoate or use resistant varieties. Spray at flowering initiation!
Mustard harvesting: Harvest when 75% pods turn yellowish-brown, seeds rattle inside pods. Cut plants early morning. Dry 3-4 days, thresh carefully. Yield: 15-20 quintals/hectare. Oil content: 37-42%!

Urea (46% Nitrogen): Most common nitrogen fertilizer. Use for all crops during vegetative growth. Apply in splits, not all at once. Rice: 130kg/acre, Wheat: 110kg/acre, Vegetables: 40-50kg/acre. Never apply near seeds!

Urea application timing: For Wheat - 1/3 at sowing, 1/3 at first irrigation (21 days), 1/3 at second irrigation (40 days). For Rice - 1/2 at transplanting, 1/4 at tillering (21 days), 1/4 at panicle initiation (50 days)!

Neem coated urea: Urea coated with neem oil. Benefits: Slow nitrogen release (efficiency 85% vs 65% normal), reduces nitrogen loss, needs less quantity (10-15% less), better for environment. Government promoted!

Urea for vegetables: Tomato (50kg/acre in 3 splits), Potato (60kg/acre - basal + 30 days + 45 days), Onion (40kg/acre in 2 splits), Cabbage (50kg/acre in 3 splits). Apply 6 inches away from plant base!

Urea precautions: Don't apply on dry soil (water immediately after), avoid over-application (promotes pests), don't mix with SSP (nitrogen loss), apply in evening/morning (less loss), split application better than single dose!

DAP (18% N, 46% P2O5): Main phosphorus fertilizer. Apply as basal (at sowing/planting time), not in splits. Wheat: 60kg/acre, Rice: 50kg/acre, Potato: 80kg/acre. Mix in soil, don't broadcast on surface!

DAP application: Apply only at sowing/planting time! Phosphorus doesn't move in soil, so later application ineffective. For row crops: place 2-3 inches below and beside seed. For transplanted crops: mix in soil before transplanting!
DAP for different crops: Wheat (60kg/acre), Paddy (50kg/acre), Maize (50kg/acre), Cotton (40kg/acre), Vegetables (60-70kg/acre), Pulses (40kg/acre). Apply at field preparation or sowing time only!

DAP vs Urea: DAP has both N (18%) and P (46%), apply at sowing. Urea only N (46%), apply in splits during growth. Can't substitute each other! Both needed - DAP for roots/flowers, Urea for leaves/growth!

DAP precautions: Never apply as top dressing (waste), don't place touching seeds (burns), avoid excess (locks micronutrients), mix well in soil. In alkaline soils, phosphorus availability reduces - use with organic matter!

MOP (Muriate of Potash - 60% K2O): Main potassium fertilizer. Important for fruit quality, disease resistance, drought tolerance. Apply: Paddy 35kg/acre, Wheat 25kg/acre, Potato 50kg/acre, Fruits 100-150kg/tree/year!

MOP application: Apply in 2 splits - half at sowing/planting, half at flowering/fruiting stage. For fruit trees: apply in monsoon (June-July) for next season flowering. Broadcast and mix in soil, needs moisture to dissolve!

Potash benefits: Improves fruit size, color & quality. Increases sugar content in sugarcane, sweetness in fruits. Strengthens stems (prevents lodging). Improves disease resistance. Critical for potato, banana, mango, citrus!

MOP for fruit trees: Mango (1-2kg/tree in June-July), Banana (200g/plant in 8 splits monthly), Citrus (1kg/tree/year in 3 splits), Pomegranate (500g/plant at flowering + fruit development). Apply 1 feet away from trunk!

MOP precautions: Don't apply near seed (salt damage), avoid in saline soils (increases salinity), can't substitute with DAP/Urea. Deficiency signs: brown leaf edges, weak stems, small fruits, poor color!

NPK Complex fertilizers: Contains all three nutrients (N-P-K). Common grades: 10-26-26 (DAP equivalent), 20-20-0 (Ammonium phosphate), 12-32-16, 19-19-19. Easier application, balanced nutrition. Apply as basal dose at planting!

NPK ratios explained: First number = Nitrogen (leaf growth), Second = Phosphorus (roots, flowers), Third = Potassium (fruits, disease resistance). Example: 19-19-19 = equal parts, good for all crops. 10-26-26 = high P for flowering crops!

NPK for vegetables: Leafy (Spinach, lettuce): high N like 20-10-10. Fruiting (Tomato, pepper): balanced 19-19-19 or high K like 10-10-20. Root (Potato, onion): high P like 10-20-10. Adjust based on growth stage!

Common NPK grades: 10-26-26 (general purpose, basal), 20-20-0 (wheat, cereals), 12-32-16 (high phosphorus crops), 19-19-19 (all-purpose, vegetables), 14-35-14 (flowering crops). Choose based on crop need and soil test!

NPK application: Broadcast and incorporate before planting for field crops. Band placement 2-3 inches beside and below seed for row crops. For vegetables: apply at bed preparation + top dress with urea later!

Organic fertilizers: FYM (0.5% N, 0.2% P, 0.5% K) - 10-15 tons/hectare, Vermicompost (1.5% N, 1% P, 1% K) - 2-3 tons/hectare, Neem cake (5% N, pest control) - 200kg/hectare. Slow release, improves soil health!

FYM (Farm Yard Manure): Well-decomposed cow dung + urine + bedding material. Apply 15-20 tons/hectare. Benefits: improves soil structure, water holding, microbial activity. Apply 2-3 weeks before planting. Not enough alone for commercial farming!

Vermicompost: Premium organic fertilizer (earthworm castings). NPK 1.5-1-1 approximately. Use 2-3 tons/hectare or 10% of potting mix. Benefits: growth hormones, enzymes, beneficial bacteria. Perfect for organic vegetables, seedlings!

Jeevamrut (liquid organic): 10kg cow dung + 10L cow urine + 2kg jaggery + 2kg pulse flour + 1kg soil in 200L water. Ferment 7 days. Apply 200L/acre with irrigation. Improves soil biology, available nutrients!

Green manure crops: Dhaincha (Sesbania) - 50kg/hectare, sow before monsoon, incorporate at flowering (45 days). Sunhemp (25kg/hectare). Cowpea (30kg/hectare). Fix nitrogen, add organic matter. Best for rice before transplanting!

Micronutrients: Zinc, Iron, Manganese, Copper, Boron, Molybdenum. Small quantity but essential! Zinc most deficient in rice & wheat. Iron in alkaline soils. Apply via soil or foliar spray for quick correction!

Zinc deficiency: Rice (khaira disease) - stunted growth, brown spots on leaves. Wheat - white/yellow leaves. Solution: Soil application - ZnSO4 25kg/hectare. Foliar spray - 0.5% ZnSO4 + 0.25% lime (prevents leaf burn)!

Iron deficiency: Young leaves turn yellow (chlorosis), veins stay green. Common in alkaline soils (pH>7.5). Solution: Foliar spray Ferrous sulfate 0.5% or Chelated iron (FeEDTA) 0.2%. Repeat 2-3 times at 10-day intervals!

Boron deficiency: Hollow stem in cauliflower, heart rot in beet, fruit drop in tomato, poor grain filling in wheat. Solution: Soil application - Borax 10kg/hectare (once in 3 years). Foliar spray - 0.2% borax!

Micronutrient spray: Multi-micronutrient mixture (Zn, Fe, Mn, B, Mo) - 2.5kg in 500L water per hectare. Spray at critical growth stages (tillering, flowering, grain filling). Add wetting agent. Spray morning/evening!

Rice Blast (most serious): Fungal disease. Leaf blast - spindle-shaped spots with gray center, brown margin. Neck blast - graying of neck, grain doesn't fill. Favored by high nitrogen, cloudy weather, 25-28°C temperature!

Blast disease control: Preventive spray - Tricyclazole 75% WP @ 0.6g/L or Carbendazim 0.1% at tillering, booting, heading stages. Curative - Kasugamycin + copper oxychloride. Spray 3 times at 10-day intervals!

Blast management: Use resistant varieties (Pusa 1121, Pusa Basmati 1509), balanced fertilization (avoid excess nitrogen), spray Tricyclazole before monsoon, don't let water stagnate, remove infected plants!

Neck blast treatment: Most damaging stage! Appears during heading/flowering. Entire panicle becomes white (blank grains). Spray Azoxystrobin + Difenoconazole at 50% flowering. Second spray after 10 days!

Blast prevention: Seed treatment with Carbendazim (2g/kg seeds), avoid late nitrogen application, silicon application (improves resistance), maintain 2-3cm water depth (not more), use disease-free seeds!

Bacterial Blight (BLB): Serious bacterial disease of rice. Symptoms: Yellow to white lesions on leaf margins/tips, wavy pattern. Kresek phase - rapid wilting of young plants. Spreads through water, wind, infected seeds!

BLB control: Use resistant varieties (Pusa Basmati 1509, Improved Pusa Basmati 1, Pusa 1121), seed treatment with Streptocycline (25ppm for 24hrs), spray Copper oxychloride 0.3% + Streptocycline 100ppm!

Bacterial blight management: Don't apply excess nitrogen (promotes disease), drain water for 3-4 days after transplanting, avoid injury to plants, spray Plantomycin or Agrimycin (100ppm) at tillering & booting!

BLB prevention: Use disease-free certified seeds, avoid deep water (5-7cm enough), balanced fertilization (excess N increases susceptibility), crop rotation with non-host crops, remove infected stubbles after harvest!

Chemical control BLB: Streptocycline 9% + Tetracycline 1% SP (3g in 10L water), or Copper hydroxide 77% WP (3g/L). Spray 2-3 times at 10-day intervals starting from tillering. Mix with wetting agent for better coverage!

Stem Borer (Yellow/White): Most destructive rice pest! Symptoms: Dead heart (young stage - central shoot dries), White head (reproductive stage - panicle turns white, no grain). Caterpillar bores into stem!
Stem borer control: Cartap hydrochloride 4G (10kg/hectare at active tillering), Chlorantraniliprole 0.4G (4kg/acre), or spray Chlorpyriphos 20EC (2ml/L) at tillering. Repeat if needed after 15 days!

Stem borer management: Use light traps (moths attracted), remove alternate hosts (grasses), keep clean bunds, pheromone traps (Scirpophaga - 8/acre), release egg parasitoid Trichogramma (50,000/acre)!

Stem borer spray: Cartap hydrochloride 50SP (1g/L), or Fipronil 5SC (2ml/L), or Chlorantraniliprole 18.5SC (0.3ml/L). Spray at early vegetative stage (within 30 days). Target leaf whorl and water surface!

Prevention: Early transplanting (escape peak borer population), clip seedling tips before transplanting (removes eggs), avoid ratoon cropping, summer plowing (exposes larvae to sun), use resistant varieties (Swarna Sub1)!

Brown Plant Hopper (BPH): Serious rice pest! Sucks sap from stem base. Symptoms: Yellowing, wilting, hopper burn (patches turn brown as if burned). Also transmits viruses. Nymphs & adults brown colored, cluster at stem base!

BPH control: Imidacloprid 17.8 SL (0.5ml/L), or Buprofezin 25SC (1.5ml/L), or Pymetrozine 50WG (0.6g/L). Spray at lower portion of plant and water surface. Avoid prophylactic spraying (creates resistance)!

BPH management: Don't use excess nitrogen (attracts BPH), maintain thin water layer during vegetative stage (exposes to predators), conserve natural enemies (spiders, mirid bugs), use resistant varieties (Swarna Sub1)!

Economic Threshold Level (ETL) for BPH: 10-15 hoppers per hill at vegetative stage, 5-10 per hill at reproductive stage. Spray only when ETL reached, not routinely! Overuse of pesticides increases BPH problems!

BPH resistant varieties: Vikramarya, DRR Dhan 45, Improve Sambha Mahsuri, CR Dhan 800. Use resistant varieties in endemic areas. Rotate pesticides to prevent resistance. Thiamethoxam as seedling root dip!

Yellow Rust (Stripe Rust): Most serious wheat disease! Yellow-orange pustules in stripes on leaves. Spreads rapidly in cool (10-15°C), humid weather. Reduce yield 40-50%! Early infection (Dec-Jan) most damaging!

Yellow rust control: Propiconazole 25EC (1ml/L), or Tebuconazole 25WG (1g/L), or Trifloxystrobin + Tebuconazole (0.5ml/L). Spray when 5-10% plants infected. Repeat after 15 days if needed. 2 sprays maximum!

Rust management: Use resistant varieties (PBW 725, HD 3086, DBW 187), timely sowing (Nov 1-15, late sowing escapes disease), balanced fertilization, avoid excess nitrogen, remove volunteer wheat plants!

Preventive spray: If rust history in area, spray Sulfex (Sulfur) 2g/L at tillering stage. Or Mancozeb 2.5g/L. For confirmed infection, use Triazole fungicides (Propiconazole, Tebuconazole). Spray in morning/evening!

Resistant varieties: HD 3086 (rust resistant, heat tolerant), PBW 725 (stripe rust resistant), DBW 187 (irrigated areas), WH 1124 (dual rust resistant). Use certified seeds, follow recommended practices!

Powdery Mildew: White powdery coating on leaves, stems, flowers. Common on cucurbits (pumpkin, cucumber), peas, mango. Doesn't need water on leaves! Spreads through air. Reduces photosynthesis, weakens plants!

Powdery mildew control: Sulfur 80WP (2g/L), or Hexaconazole 5EC (2ml/L), or Azoxystrobin 23SC (1ml/L). Spray at first appearance. Repeat every 7-10 days. Spray both leaf surfaces. 3-4 sprays may be needed!
Cultural control: Proper spacing (air circulation), avoid overhead irrigation, remove infected parts, don't apply excess nitrogen, grow in sunny locations, resistant varieties when available!
Home remedy: Milk spray (1:10 milk:water) or Baking soda spray (1 tablespoon + 1 teaspoon oil per liter). Spray weekly. Works for mild infections on home gardens. Commercial farms need fungicides!
Prevention: Plant resistant varieties, avoid crowding, prune for air circulation, water at base not leaves, apply Sulfur or Potassium bicarbonate preventively in disease-prone areas!

Aphids (Chepti): Small soft-bodied insects (green, black, brown). Suck sap from tender parts. Secrete honeydew (attracts ants, black fungus). Transmit virus diseases. Multiply rapidly! Common on mustard, cotton, vegetables!

Aphid control: Imidacloprid 17.8SL (0.5ml/L), or Thiamethoxam 25WG (0.5g/L), or Dimethoate 30EC (2ml/L). Spray thoroughly on leaf underside. One spray usually sufficient. Avoid during flowering (affects bees)!

Natural control: Spray water forcefully (dislodges aphids), neem oil 3ml/L, soap solution (5g/L). Encourage natural enemies - ladybird beetles, lacewings, syrphid flies. They control aphids naturally!
Mustard aphid: Peak infestation Jan-Feb. Spray Dimethoate 2ml/L or Imidacloprid 0.5ml/L when 10% plants infested. One spray at flowering initiation. Don't spray during flowering (bee activity)!

Prevention: Yellow sticky traps, reflective mulch (aluminum foil confuses aphids), companion planting (garlic, onion), avoid excess nitrogen (promotes tender growth attractive to aphids), conserve natural enemies!

Whitefly: Tiny white flying insects. Suck sap, weaken plants, secrete honeydew. Major problem: transmit viruses (Leaf curl in chili/tomato, Yellow vein mosaic in okra). Cotton whitefly causes severe damage!

Whitefly control: Spiromesifen 22.9SC (1ml/L), or Pyriproxyfen 10EC (1ml/L), or Diafenthiuron 50WP (1g/L). Spray leaf undersides thoroughly. Mix with wetting agent. Rotate insecticides (prevent resistance)!
Cotton whitefly: Serious pest! Spray Imidacloprid 0.5ml/L or Thiamethoxam 0.5g/L at first appearance. If virus symptoms appear, spray Acetamiprid 20SP (0.5g/L). Remove infected plants immediately!

Whitefly management: Yellow sticky traps (attract adults), reflective silver mulch, remove weeds (alternate hosts), avoid late planting, use virus-resistant varieties (Chili - Kashi Anmol, Arka Tejas)!
Neem-based control: Neem oil 3ml/L + Azadirachtin 1500ppm (2ml/L). Spray weekly. Works better as preventive. For severe infestation, use chemical insecticides. Mix with sticker for better adherence!

Fruit borers (Helicoverpa armigera): Caterpillar bores into fruits/pods. Damages tomato, okra, chili, pigeon pea, chickpea. Young larvae greenish, older brownish. Single larva damages multiple fruits!
Fruit borer control: Emamectin benzoate 5SG (0.5g/L), or Spinosad 45SC (0.3ml/L), or Indoxacarb 14.5SC (1ml/L). Spray at flower initiation, repeat at 10-15 day intervals. 3-4 sprays needed!
Integrated Management: Pheromone traps (4-5/acre, replace lure monthly), NPV spray (250LE/ha with 2.5kg jaggery), neem seed kernel extract (5%), bird perches, grow marigold/coriander (trap crops)!
Tomato fruit borer: Monitor daily, handpick larvae & damaged fruits. Spray Chlorantraniliprole 18.5SC (0.3ml/L) or Flubendiamide 20WG (0.25g/L) at flowering. Rotate insecticides (prevent resistance)!

Organic control: Bt spray (Bacillus thuringiensis - 2g/L), NSKE (Neem Seed Kernel Extract - 5%), NPV (Nuclear Polyhedrosis Virus - 250LE/ha). Spray in evening. Release Trichogramma egg parasitoids (50,000/acre)!
Termites (Deemak): Underground soil insects. Damage roots, seeds, stems, wooden structures. Major problem in sugarcane, wheat, maize, trees. Prefer organic matter. More active in summer, light soils!
Termite control: Chlorpyriphos 20EC (2.5L in 400L water per hectare, drench soil around plants), or Fipronil 5SC (2L/ha as soil application). Apply before sowing or with first irrigation!
Sugarcane termite: Treat setts with Chlorpyriphos (2.5ml/L) before planting. Soak 10 minutes. Or apply Chlorpyriphos 2.5L/ha mixed with irrigation water at planting. Earthing up helps reduce damage!

Termite prevention: Deep summer plowing (exposes colonies to sun), remove crop residue, avoid fresh organic matter at sowing (attracts termites), use well-decomposed FYM, soil application of Fipronil 0.3G (15kg/ha)!

Organic methods: Wood ash application in soil, neem cake (200kg/ha), castor cake. Destroy termite mounds near fields. Flooding fields where possible. Plant trap crops (sugarcane stubbles) and destroy!
Root-knot Nematodes: Microscopic worms in soil. Attack roots, form galls/knots. Reduce nutrient uptake, stunt growth, yellow leaves. Major problem in tomato, okra, banana, papaya, vegetables!
Nematode control: Carbofuran 3G (1kg/acre at planting), or Phorate 10G (10kg/acre). Mix in soil around root zone. Bio-control: Paecilomyces lilacinus (5kg/acre with FYM). Neem cake 200kg/acre!
Cultural management: Crop rotation with non-host crops (maize, sorghum, grasses), summer plowing (expose to sun), flooding fields, grow marigold (African marigold variety - traps & kills nematodes)!

Banana nematode: Serious problem! Topple/fall over during fruiting. Use nematode-free tissue culture plants. Apply Carbofuran 3G (50g/plant in root zone) every 3 months. Mulching with neem/marigold leaves helps!

Resistant varieties: Tomato - Pusa Sheetal (root-knot resistant), Okra - Arka Anamika, Brinjal - IIHR-6. Use organic amendments (neem cake 200kg/ha). Green manuring with mustard/sunhemp reduces nematodes!

Drip Irrigation: Water directly to root zone through drippers. Water saving 40-70%! Increases yield 20-50%. Uniform water distribution. Allows fertigation. Best for: vegetables, fruits, sugarcane, cotton!

Drip components: Water source → Pump → Filter (screen/disc) → Fertilizer tank → Main line (PVC) → Sub-main → Lateral (drip lines) → Drippers (4LPH most common). Need pressure regulator for hilly areas!

Drip spacing: Vegetables (row crops): Lateral spacing 1.5-2ft, dripper spacing 30-40cm. Widely spaced crops (tomato, cotton): Lateral 5-6ft, dripper 50-60cm. Closely spaced (onion, garlic): Inline drip, drippers 20-30cm!

Drip installation cost: Approximately ₹45,000-60,000 per acre (including pump, filter, mainline, laterals, drippers). Subsidy available 55-90% depending on state and farmer category. Check with agriculture department!

Drip maintenance: Clean filters weekly, check drippers for clogging, flush system regularly (open lateral ends), apply acid treatment yearly (remove scaling), replace laterals every 4-5 years. Use filtered water!

Sprinkler Irrigation: Mimics rainfall. Suitable for all crops, all soil types. Water saving 30-40%. Types: Mini sprinkler (radius 4-6m, vegetables/fruits), Medium (8-12m, field crops), Rain gun (30-50m radius, large fields)!

Sprinkler types: 1) Mini sprinkler (colored types - vegetables, banana), 2) Micro sprinkler (spacing 4x4m, orchards), 3) Medium sprinkler (wheat, mustard - 12x12m), 4) Rain gun (sugarcane - 18x18m or more)!

Sprinkler cost: Mini sprinkler - ₹30,000-40,000/acre, Medium sprinkler - ₹25,000-35,000/acre, Rain gun - ₹40,000-50,000/acre. Government subsidy 50-80% available. Cheaper than drip, suitable for cereals!

Sprinkler for wheat: Spacing 12m x 12m or 15m x 15m. Medium pressure sprinkler (2-3 kg/cm² pressure). Apply 50mm water per irrigation. Saves water 30-35%, increases yield, reduces labor. Good for large fields!

Sprinkler vs Drip: Drip - Row crops, vegetables, fruits, water saving 50-70%, expensive, fertigation easy. Sprinkler - All crops, cereals, pulses, water saving 30-40%, cheaper, suitable for wheat/mustard/chickpea!

Mulching: Covering soil with organic (straw, leaves) or inorganic (plastic) material. Benefits: Moisture conservation 30-40%, weed control, soil temperature moderation, improved yield! Widely used in vegetables, fruits!

Plastic mulch: Black (most common - weed control, heat absorption), Silver (pest repellent, heat reflection), White (cool season), Transparent (soil solarization). Black mulch increases tomato yield 40-60%!

Organic mulch: Paddy straw (best, cheap - ₹2-3/kg), sugarcane trash, dry leaves, wood chips, grass clippings. Apply 5-7cm thick layer. Decomposes, adds organic matter. Need to replenish. Good for fruit trees!

Mulching in vegetables: Lay plastic mulch on raised beds before transplanting, make holes for planting. Drip irrigation under mulch. Black mulch for tomato, capsicum, brinjal. Silver for cucurbits (repels aphids/whitefly)!

Mulching cost: Plastic mulch (25 micron, 1.2m width) - ₹15,000-20,000/acre including laying. Paddy straw mulch - ₹8,000-12,000/acre. Increases net profit despite cost (higher yield, reduced irrigation/weeding)!

Soil Testing: Essential for balanced fertilization! Tests: pH, organic carbon, available N-P-K, micronutrients. Collect samples before planting. Test every 2-3 years. Free at government labs! Get Soil Health Card!

Soil sample collection: Collect from 8-10 spots in field, 6-8 inch depth, mix well, take 500g sample. Avoid manure heaps, water channels, field boundaries. Air dry, pack in cloth bag. Label with name & location!

Soil testing labs: Government agriculture offices (Krishi Vigyan Kendra - KVK, District Agriculture Office), State agriculture universities. Testing FREE at government labs! Private labs charge ₹100-500. Results in 7-15 days!

Soil Health Card: Government scheme - FREE soil testing every 2 years. Card shows soil nutrients, recommendations for fertilizer use. Apply online at soilhealth.dac.gov.in or contact agriculture office!

Interpreting results: Low N (add urea/FYM), Low P (add DAP/SSP), Low K (add MOP), pH<5.5 (add lime 500kg/acre), pH>8 (add gypsum 500kg/acre). Follow recommendations on Soil Health Card for fertilizer doses!

Seed Treatment: Treating seeds before sowing with fungicide/insecticide/bio-agents. Benefits: Protects from soil-borne diseases, improves germination, early vigor, better establishment! Cheap investment, high returns!

Fungicide seed treatment: Rice - Carbendazim or Tricyclazole 2g/kg seeds. Wheat - Vitavax Power (Carboxin + Thiram) 2.5g/kg. Cotton - Imidacloprid + Carbendazim (10ml + 2g per kg). Soak 24 hours or dust dry!
Biological seed treatment: Trichoderma viride (4g/kg seed with starch solution), Pseudomonas fluorescens (10g/kg), Azospirillum + PSB (each 25g/kg for pulses). Organic alternative to chemicals!
Seed priming: Soak seeds in water 8-12 hours, shade dry to original moisture. Benefits: Faster germination, uniform emergence, better seedling vigor. Useful for old seeds, direct-seeded rice/maize!

Seed treatment method: Dry dressing - mix seeds with powder chemical in poly bag. Wet treatment - dissolve chemical in minimum water, coat seeds, dry in shade. Always use recommended dose, don't over-treat!

Greenhouse/Polyhouse: Controlled environment cultivation. Protects from weather extremes, pests. Grow high-value crops year-round. Types: Naturally ventilated (cheaper), Fan-pad cooled (expensive, controlled). Vegetables, flowers, nursery!

Polyhouse cost: Naturally ventilated - ₹700-900/m² (₹28-35 lakh/acre), Fan-pad cooled - ₹1400-1800/m² (₹56-72 lakh/acre). Government subsidy 50-90% under protected cultivation scheme. Check with Horticulture Department!
Greenhouse crops: Tomato (yield 150-200 tons/ha vs 50-60 open field), Capsicum (export quality, ₹1.5-2.5 lakh/1000m² profit), Cucumber, Rose, Gerbera, Seedling nursery. Need training before starting!

Greenhouse management: Temperature control (vents, fans, fogging), Humidity (60-70%), Drip irrigation + fertigation, Soilless cultivation (Cocopeat, perlite), IPM (sticky traps, bio-control). Regular monitoring crucial!

Greenhouse tomato: Indeterminate hybrids (Abhinav, US-618, Vaishali). Spacing 45x45cm, single stem training, 12-14 months crop, 3-4 harvests. Yield 15-20kg/plant. Need pruning, training, pollination (bumblebees or vibrator)!

Hydroponics: Soilless cultivation, plants grown in nutrient solution. Faster growth, higher yield, less water (90% saving), no soil-borne diseases! Systems: NFT (Nutrient Film Technique), DWC (Deep Water Culture), Dutch bucket!

Hydroponic setup cost: Small scale (100m²) - ₹3-5 lakh, Commercial (1000m²) - ₹25-40 lakh (NFT system). Includes structure, grow channels, nutrient tanks, pumps, monitoring equipment. Lettuce, herbs most profitable!
Hydroponic crops: Lettuce (ready 30-35 days, 4-5kg/m²/month), Tomato (NFT/Dutch bucket, 60-80kg/m²/year), Cucumber, Capsicum, Herbs (basil, mint, coriander), Strawberry, Spinach!

Nutrient management: Use commercial hydroponic nutrient (A&B solutions - NPK + micronutrients). EC (Electrical Conductivity): Lettuce 1.2-1.8, Tomato 2.0-3.5. pH: 5.5-6.5. Monitor daily with EC/pH meters!
Hydroponics training: Contact ICAR institutes, State agriculture universities, Private companies (Hosachiguru, LetUs Grow). 5-7 day training costs ₹15,000-25,000. Essential before commercial setup!

Vermicompost: Premium organic fertilizer made by earthworms (Eisenia fetida - red worms). NPK approximately 1.5-2-1.5 + growth hormones. Improves soil health, water holding, beneficial microbes. Use 2-3 tons/hectare!

Vermicompost making: Cement tank/HDPE bed (10x3x2 ft). Layer: 6-inch cow dung (semi-decomposed) → 3-inch farm waste → release worms (2000/bed) → cover with gunny bag → spray water daily → ready 60-70 days!

Vermicompost worms: Eisenia fetida (red worms/tiger worms). Buy from KVK/agriculture office (₹400-600 per kg, ~1500 worms). Feed on cow dung, kitchen waste, farm residue. Multiply rapidly. Can't use regular earthworms!

Vermicompost business: Production cost ₹4-6/kg, selling price ₹12-18/kg. From 10x3ft bed: 150-200kg per batch (70 days). Set up 10-20 beds for commercial production. Market through agriculture offices, nurseries, online!

Vermicompost use: Mix 10-20% in potting soil. Field application 2-3 tons/hectare before planting. For vegetables: 1-2 tons/acre. Seedling mix: 30% vermicompost + 70% soil. Tea (liquid): 1kg in 10L water, filter, spray!
